notes.meaning: Hannah responds to God's gift of a son with a joyful song of praise. Her horn being lifted high means God restored her strength and dignity after years of being mocked. She rejoices not just in her newborn boy, but in the Lord who saves and protects the helpless.

Hannah proclaims that the Lord alone is perfectly holy, with no equal in all creation. Calling God a rock shows that He is an unshakeable shelter that never crumbles. True stability comes only from trusting in Him.

Arrogant people are told to stop boasting and belittling others. God knows every secret thought, and He weighs human actions on a scale of perfect justice. No one can hide their true motives from His sight.

Human strength can fail in an instant, breaking the weapons of the most skilled warriors. At the same time, God gives new energy and courage to those who are exhausted and stumbling. Real victory comes from God's power, not human might.

Those who once had plenty of food can find themselves working long hours just to eat, while the starving are filled. A childless woman receives a full family of children, while the woman who boasted of many sons ends up lonely. God easily overturns human fortunes according to His wise purposes.

The Lord holds complete authority over human life and death. He can bring people down near the grave, into deep despair, and He can restore them to life and health. Every breath we take is in His hands.

Wealth and poverty are directed by God's providence rather than blind luck. He lowers the self-reliant and lifts up those who are bowed low. This truth reminds us to remain humble when prosperous and hopeful when facing hard times.

God reaches down to lift the poorest beggars from the dirt and seats them among rulers. He has the right to do this because He created the earth and holds up its foundations like pillars. Since the entire universe belongs to Him, He can change any person's position as He pleases.

The Lord guides and protects the steps of those who remain faithful to Him. Those who turn to wickedness end up ruined and silenced in spiritual darkness. No human being can win against God through sheer personal power.

Those who fight against the Lord will be shattered when He thunders in majesty against them. Hannah looks ahead to a day when God will judge the entire world and empower His chosen king. This marks the first time Scripture uses the title of God's anointed, pointing directly forward to the Messiah.

Elkanah and Hannah returned home to Ramah after finishing their worship at Shiloh. The young child Samuel stayed behind to assist the high priest Eli in the daily duties of the sanctuary. Even at a very young age, Samuel was already learning how to serve God faithfully.

Eli's sons were corrupt men who did not truly know or respect the Lord. Even though they worked as priests, they had no real love for God or His laws. They treated their sacred roles as nothing more than a way to gain personal power and pleasure.

God's law gave priests certain set portions of a peace offering, but Eli's sons invented their own greedy tradition. While the worshiper was boiling the rest of the meat for a fellowship meal, the priest's servant would show up holding a large three-pronged fork. They pushed aside God's rules to grab extra food for themselves.

The servant plunged the fork into the pot and took whatever meat stuck to it for the priests. They carried out this theft against every Israelite family who traveled to worship at Shiloh. Their greed turned a sacred feast of gratitude into an occasion for robbery.

The priests committed an even worse offense by demanding raw meat before the animal fat was burned on the altar. The law required the fat to be offered on the fire to God first as His holy portion. By taking meat ahead of time to roast, they showed that their own appetites mattered more to them than God's honor.

When ordinary worshipers asked the servant to wait until God's portion was burned on the altar, the servant threatened to take the meat by force. The common people showed far more reverence for God than the priests did. Eli's sons relied on bullying and intimidation inside the house of God.

The behavior of Eli's sons was a terrible sin because it treated the Lord's holy offerings with open contempt. Their greed made ordinary Israelites hate coming to worship at the sanctuary. Ungodly leaders create an awful stumbling block for people seeking God.

In direct contrast to the corrupt priests, the boy Samuel served the Lord with an innocent heart. He was dressed in a linen ephod, a simple garment worn by sacred workers in the tabernacle. Samuel remained pure even while surrounded by bad examples.

Each year, Hannah stitched a small robe for Samuel and brought it with her to the annual sacrifice at Shiloh. She continued to express her deep love for him as he grew older year by year. This yearly gift showed her quiet and faithful support of his sacred service.

Eli spoke a blessing over Elkanah and Hannah whenever they brought their yearly offering. He asked the Lord to give Hannah more children to take the place of the son she had given away to God's house. After receiving this blessing, the parents returned home in peace.

The Lord answered Eli's blessing, and Hannah gave birth to three more sons and two daughters. Meanwhile, young Samuel continued to grow under God's personal care in the tabernacle courts. God shows that no one ever loses out by offering their dearest treasures to Him.

As Eli grew very old, reports kept coming to him about the shameless sins his sons were committing across Israel. They were even sleeping with the women who assisted at the entrance of the tabernacle. Their actions dragged the holy worship of God down into pagan immorality.

Eli questioned his sons about why they were committing such wicked deeds that had become common gossip among all the people. Yet his response was far too soft and came only as words without any real discipline. As high priest and judge, he should have removed them from their office immediately.

Eli urged his sons to stop, warning them that the reports circulating among God's people were terrible. By their sinful behavior, the priests were leading the entire nation into disobedience. Weak warnings are never enough to put an end to bold rebellion.

Eli warned that when people sin against each other, a judge can settle the dispute, but no human referee can step between a willful sinner and God. His sons ignored his words because the Lord had already decided to bring about their judgment. Their long habit of sin had brought them to a place of total ruin.

differ.view: God actively hardened their hearts and withheld repentance as a just decree of judgment for their stubborn rebellion.
Their refusal to listen came from their own willful disobedience, which had finally crossed into the point of certain doom.

notes.meaning: In bright contrast to Eli's corrupt family, the boy Samuel grew in both physical stature and spiritual grace. He found favor in the eyes of the Lord and earned the respect of the people around him. His childhood pointed forward to how Jesus Himself would grow in favor with God and people.

An unnamed prophet came to Eli carrying a stern message directly from the Lord. God reminded Eli of how He had made Himself known to Aaron's family while they were still slaves under Pharaoh in Egypt. God had shown them great grace long before they had any prestige.

God reminded Eli that He had chosen Aaron's family above all the other tribes to offer sacrifices, burn incense, and wear the sacred priestly vestments. The Lord had also provided generously for them by giving them portions from the altar offerings. Treating such holy gifts lightly was an act of deep ingratitude.

The prophet accused Eli of trampling on God's offerings and honoring his own sons more than God. Eli enjoyed eating the fattened meats his sons stole, and he refused to discipline them out of fear of upsetting them. Putting family loyalty ahead of obedience to God is an insult to the Lord.

God had once promised that Eli's family line would serve as priests before Him continually, but their open contempt broke that agreement. The Lord declared that He will honor those who honor Him, while those who look down on Him will be treated as worthless. Eli's family had taken God's favor for granted, and now that privilege was being taken away.

God warned that He would cut off the strength and authority of Eli's family line. A person's arm stood for power and influence in Hebrew thinking. Because of their wickedness, no man in Eli's household would ever live long enough to reach old age.

Eli would live to see distress fall heavily upon God's sacred dwelling place. Even while the rest of Israel experienced blessings, Eli's household would face constant grief, and none of his descendants would reach old age. This began to happen when the tabernacle was shattered and the ark was lost.

Any descendant of Eli who survived to serve at the altar would live in deep grief and misery. The rest of his family line would die early in the prime of life. God's judgment would stand as a lasting warning about the cost of corrupting holy office.

God gave Eli an unmistakable sign to prove that every word of this prophecy would surely come to pass. His two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, would both die on the very same day. When this took place on the battlefield, Eli knew the rest of the judgment was unavoidable.

The Lord promised to raise up a faithful priest who would obey His heart and mind completely. God pledged to build this priest an enduring family line that would walk before His anointed king forever. This was partly fulfilled through Zadok during King Solomon's reign, and ultimately through Jesus Christ, our eternal High Priest.

The surviving members of Eli's family would eventually bow down to the new priestly line, begging for small coins and scraps of bread. They would plead for any humble chore around the sanctuary just to have enough food to stay alive. The family that once greedily demanded the finest cuts of meat would end up begging for a single crust.
